spans.text: Rustle rustle...
Creeeak... The two slip into the apartment, making as little noise as possible.
Is there anyone inside?
Relax, I checked. Those people are long gone.
People only get fired up about the news for a day or two. Time is the best sedative.
She flips on the light switch and the room immediately brightens up.
Ahhhh~ There's no place like home!
But you're still going down to the lab tomorrow, right?
Of course! They finally opened the place back up again. Granted, it's just to tell everyone that they're fired...
Yeah, I'll go tidy up the house. You'd better hurry up if you want to contact that agent. You need to be up bright and early tomorrow.
Okay.
Click. The call goes through, and she is answered by a lazy-sounding voice.
Good news?
...There's news, but whether or not it's good is up to you.
About the truck—it was definitely from Galatea, but there are many such vehicles. Also each truck makes a lot of trips, so the transport logs alone are several hundred pages long.
What information do those logs contain?
My clearance only gives me access to names, warehouses, times and so on—basic stuff.
And the system doesn't let me do open searches.
Speaking of names, I have a piece of info for you.
The consignee is called "Umruss".
Come to think of it, you've got a technical department, right?
Can't you do something to boost my access clearance?
If we could do that, why not just hack your intranet directly?
That sort of thing leaves traces, Frau Informant.
Alright, I'll try to think of something else.
Does Gray Elementary only take first-grade students?
Get some of your seniors to help, Frau Nele.
Wait, are you suggesting that I use other people's...
I didn't say anything.
...Yes, you said nothing at all.
What about the mansion?
Same thing. I don't have access.
...Alright then. I can't count on you for everything, after all.
...I'll do my best.
Anyone can say that.
Right, I've got stuff to do on my end. Talk to you later.
Nele hangs up and exhales heavily.
Nele, you're a scientist, not a spy.
I brought this on myself...
Whew... I'll go check again tomorrow.
Don't push yourself too hard. You're just an ordinary girl.
Relax, Mia. I've got this.
Nele puts her communicator away and pulls her coat over her body as Mia watches on with concern.
Hi~ Herr Eicher.
...Nele? What are you doing here?
The researcher who's about to leave is surprised to see Nele as she enters the workroom.
I thought you'd already...
I just came to get some things. I left some personal items here.
I see...
Well, Professor Iverson's finished handing his work over. We'll be having a farewell dinner later with Sara and Melanie. Are you coming?
Uh... Sure.
I'll leave the lights on for you. Make sure you turn them off when you go.
See you at the pantry later.
Okay.
After smiling and waving goodbye to Eicher, Nele goes up to her computer.
Logging in to the Gray Institute of Biology Database—
"Umruss"—begin search.
Huh? There's only one entry!
The red underline means that it is highly classified.
Good thing I'm using Professor Iverson's card...
Hmm... Now then...
Gray—the teacher who shone a light on her life.
Mrs. Gray, to me, you are like a fire that illuminates a traveler's path.
If you ARE innocent, then I won't let anyone besmirch you.
Got it!
There are org charts, meeting minutes, schedules and diaries—
Her heart begins to pound.
...A project direction change meeting... on May 22nd?
Looks like that was before I came in.
Knock knock knock.
I forgot my scarf.
Oh yeah, two people are already here, make sure you hurry.
...Okay, give me 5 minutes.
Nele minimizes the window with a perfectly even expression and greets the person who came in.
Eicher gets his scarf and closes the door once again.
Whew... That scared the hell out of me.
She enters the server again and looks at the personnel records again. Gray's vivacious face looks back at her.
Nele's hands tremble.
Mrs. Gray wasn't in the lab that day!
As for her carpool records... Sh-she went to...Neu-Tempelhof...
Knock knock knock.
—There is a knocking on the door once again.
Nele! Everyone's here, are you done yet?
Y-yes, I am, I'm coming right now.
Nele silently turns off her computer and enters the pantry with a big smile. Then she returns her "borrowed" card to its owner, who is none the wiser.
Let's head out!
The waiter brings out a tray laden with sausage platters and beer.
So, will you be going to that research institute in Bremen, Professor Iverson?
Yeah, they have an immunology project there too.
They're asking if I want to bring my team with me. Any takers?
My family lives here, so moving to another city would be too much of a pain.
(Sighs) I haven't even finished a full year here, it's going to look bad on my resume.
Well, everyone's spent pretty much the same amount of time here, so don't worry, we can be witnesses for each other's background checks.
Also, they gave us a pretty hefty severance package, so we can take half a year to slowly find new work.
Still, I'm kind of interested in the Bremen position. They're more developed than Berlin, so they'll probably be able to get bigger grants.
Yeah, they're quite generous with their salaries.
It's worth it no matter how much they pay us.
After all, we're the only ones in the industry with exclusive first-hand information.
Oh no, animal trials are a far cry from human trials.
Yup~ As they say, the best scientists are often the mad ones.
First-hand "information"? Do you mean Idunn?
I noticed quite a few companies seem to have special anti-ELID projects going on a while back.
Yes, and Gray is one of the leaders in the field.
There are hundreds, if not thousands of companies that want to start projects like that, and there are dozens who already have.
But she's the only one that has been able to push a project this far.
For starters, our research is 90% finalized.
Yeah, so all that's left are the Phase III trials. I can't think of why it would have resulted in brain death. Fortunately the final tests showed that they were fine.
Huh? What... What's wrong?
You didn't know?
When I saw the news, I thought someone stole your serum. Did you really not know?
...What should I know?
...That serum's not meant to be used outside the lab.
Nele puts down her cup and tenses up.
Why?
Oh boy... I can't believe you actually don't know... Should we tell her...Or not?
But that was the direction they were going with when we came in. How could you NOT have known when you joined?
(I need to get to the bottom of this... )
Come to think of it, there was an NDA, but I didn't have the time to read through the whole thing.
Her heart pounds faster and faster... The truth hidden in the mists all this while is about to be revealed—
No wonder you didn't know.
At your next job, make sure you finish reading the NDA before signing your contract!
Thank you for the reminder.
So, what is it?
I'm talking about the direction of our research. We're not working towards treatment, but selection.
We're using the human immune system to select for the most appropriate antibodies.
Isn't that killing people?
Nele's voice unconsciously rises by a couple of decibels.
It's SAVING people.
Nele, we're saving people.
There's no perfect treatment for ELID. You ought to know that, right?
Which is why Idunn is the salvation everyone's hoping for!
Oh, you're too naive!
We can only find a true immunosome after a great deal of experimentation. The only effective treatment is by obtaining a blood serum sample from them and replicating it.
No wonder the government took so long to approve it. Did they know what we were researching?
Of course. The publicly-stated goal of Idunn was a Tower of Babel to begin with, something that could never come true.
But when you use it as a political slogan, you can make a ton of money.
I thought Mrs. Gray explained all this to you.
How did you even make it onto the team if you can't even accept that?
I'd like to know myself!
Nele scoops up her sling bag on the bench and strides out of the hotel's private dining room, leaving a group of people looking at each other behind her.
